market_type_reason: This market is B2B because the primary buyers are hospitals, wound care clinics, and home health agencies that purchase medical equipment for clinical use.
market_definition: The global market for medical devices and accompanying dressings that utilize controlled sub-atmospheric pressure to promote healing in acute or chronic wounds.
core_scope: A core player must design, manufacture, and commercially distribute complete negative pressure wound therapy systems, including the vacuum pumps, specialized canisters, and compatible wound dressing kits.
adjacent_segments: Traditional wound care dressings like gauze, hydrocolloids, and alginates without active pressure systems
Advanced biologics and bioengineered skin substitutes used for wound closure
General surgical suction pumps and fluid aspiration systems not calibrated for wound healing
Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) chambers and equipment

market_participants.definition: Companies that design, produce, and sell their own branded NPWT devices and consumable kits to healthcare providers.
market_participants.why_relevant: They drive the technological development of the market and hold the core regulatory approvals (like FDA clearance) required to sell medical devices.

market_participants.definition: Specialized medical supply companies that purchase NPWT systems from manufacturers to manage local logistics, sales, and delivery to hospitals and clinics.
market_participants.why_relevant: They serve as the vital operational bridge between manufacturers and fragmented healthcare facilities, managing inventory and contract fulfillment.

market_participants.definition: Medical equipment rental companies that handle the cleaning, maintenance, tracking, and short-term leasing of NPWT pumps to hospitals or home care settings.
market_participants.why_relevant: Many healthcare providers prefer a rental model over capital expenditure, making fleet management services a key part of how the product reaches patients.

primary_reason: Manufacturer is the chosen role because the competitive landscape is defined by companies creating and selling their own proprietary physical medical devices, whereas distributors and service providers merely facilitate the logistics and commercialization of those devices.
